claim: Agent-first teams improve reliability by making missing capabilities legible and enforceable, not by asking agents to try harder.
locator: Redefining the role of the engineer

claim: Repository knowledge should be a small map with progressive disclosure and mechanical freshness checks.
locator: We made repository knowledge the system of record

claim: Long-running orchestration should continuously ensure active work has an agent until completion.
A coding harness is an execution loop whose context, tools, and observations determine reliability.
Codex is evaluated on full project creation, features, refactors, debugging, and review, not only short code generation.
Blocking guardrails prevent expensive model execution and side effects when a cheap gate fails.
End-to-end traces should preserve workflow, task, turn, tool, guardrail, and handoff events.
Private evals should represent the recurring patterns of the actual workflow being optimized.
Real repository tasks plus executable tests provide a reproducible agent evaluation substrate.
Benchmark tasks require feasibility review because impossible or ambiguous samples distort results.
A common task format enables repeatable long-horizon agent evaluation across tasks.
Durable execution, persistence, and human-in-the-loop are runtime properties, not prompt conventions.
Prompt instructions should be optimized against an explicit metric and dataset rather than subjective rewriting.
Program- and data-aware instruction proposals can be selected through measured downstream evaluation.
Parallel coding tasks are isolated by repository-preloaded environments and should expose progress to operators.
